title: Derived tensor-Hom adjunction for an arbitrary DG bimodule
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. Let $(A,d)$ and $(B,d)$ be such differential graded algebras. A differential graded $(A,B)$-bimodule $N$ has commuting unital graded left $A$- and right $B$-actions, with $d(an)=d(a)n+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(n)$ and $d(nb)=d(n)b+(-1)^{|n|}n\,d(b)$ for homogeneous elements. For right modules $M$ over $A$ and $Y$ over $B$, set $M\otimes_A N=(M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}N)/(ma\otimes n-m\otimes an)$, with differential $d(m\otimes n)=d(m)\otimes n+(-1)^{|m|}m\otimes d(n)$. Let $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(N,Y)$ have degree-$r$ homogeneous right $B$-linear maps, differential $d(f)=d_Yf-(-1)^rf d_N$, and right $A$-action $(fa)(n)=f(an)$. The total derived functors
$$T_N=-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N:D(A,d)\longrightarrow D(B,d),\qquad U_N=R\operatorname{Hom}_B(N,-):D(B,d)\longrightarrow D(A,d)$$
exist on the unbounded categories and are exact. The second is represented by $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(N,I)$ for a quasi-isomorphism $Y\to I$ with $I$ homotopically injective, meaning $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(C,I)$ is acyclic for every acyclic right DG $B$-module $C$; such resolutions exist. The first is the total left derived functor of the displayed balanced tensor. Chain currying $g\mapsto(m\mapsto(n\mapsto g(m\otimes n)))$ induces natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B,d)}(T_NM,Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(M,U_NY).$$
They specify an adjunction $T_N\dashv U_N$. With the canonical shift comparisons induced by tensor and Hom, its unit and counit commute with shifts; these exact functors carry distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles. No flatness, boundedness, compactness or quasi-isomorphism between $A$ and $B$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09LT, lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint; its derived tensor and Hom constructions and the canonical tensor/Hom shift comparisons in the preceding sections.

proof.text: The property-(P) resolution statement gives a quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to M$ with an exhaustive graded-split filtration whose quotients are sums of shifts of $A$. View $A$ as the one-object dg category with endomorphism complex $A$ and composition its multiplication. That filtration is exactly semi-freeness for this category, so the semi-free projectivity statement makes $P$ homotopically projective. The injective statement applied over $B$ gives $i:Y\to I$ with $I$ homotopically injective. Both constructions apply to arbitrary integer-graded modules. Localization is fully faithful on homotopically projective sources and on homotopically injective targets. Consequently a quasi-isomorphism between two projective models, or between two injective models, is an isomorphism in the homotopy category: lift its derived inverse by the stated bijection and use injectivity of that bijection to check both inverse identities.

The homotopy calculus supplies exact functors $F_N,G_N$ and their chain currying isomorphism, with the specified shift comparisons. As functors on homotopy categories they carry the isomorphisms of step 1 to isomorphisms. Therefore $Q_BF_N$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms between homotopically projective objects and $Q_AG_N$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms between homotopically injective objects. This uses no preservation of arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms by tensor or Hom.

Apply the resolving-class essential-constancy statement to $K(A,d)$, $W_A$, $Q_BF_N$ and its class of homotopically projective modules, using the compatible fraction calculus. Each denominator pro-diagram is essentially constant, which is precisely everywhere-definedness of the left derived functor in Definition 05S9. The everywhere-defined exactness statement gives its universal total left derived functor $T_N$, with $T_N(M)\cong Q_B(P\otimes_A N)$. Apply the same two statements to $K(B,d)^{\mathrm{op}}$, $W_B^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $(Q_AG_N)^{\mathrm{op}}:K(B,d)^{\mathrm{op}}\to D(A,d)^{\mathrm{op}}$, taking homotopically injective objects as the resolving class, and then take opposites. The DG localization statement makes these opposite categories triangulated, $W_B^{\mathrm{op}}$ saturated and compatible, and $Q_B^{\mathrm{op}}$ its localization; the opposite-functor statement makes $(Q_AG_N)^{\mathrm{op}}$ exact. This gives the universal total right derived functor $U_N$, with $U_N(Y)\cong Q_A\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(N,I)$. The two fraction calculi and two-out-of-three hold by the DG localization statement; step 1 supplies replacements and step 2 inversion on the classes. Opposites interchange the cone/pro and cocone/ind criteria. Both functors are exact with the derived shift comparisons induced by those of $F_N,G_N$.

source.place: Tags 06XN and 05S9 (derived.tex), 09LS and 09LI (dga.tex); derived.tex Tag 05SC via the cited exactness statement

proof.text: For the models $P\to M$ and $Y\to I$ above, form the following composite of bijections: $$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B,d)}(T_NM,Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(B,d)}(P\otimes_A N,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A,d)}(P,\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(N,I))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(M,U_NY).$$ The first uses the comparison into the homotopically injective $I$ and the isomorphism $Y\cong Q_BI$; it does not require $P\otimes_A N$ to be projective. The middle is $H^0$ of the chain currying isomorphism. The last uses the comparison out of the homotopically projective $P$ and $Q_AP\cong M$; it does not require $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(N,I)$ to be injective over $A$. This proves the asserted bijection without a flatness hypothesis on $N$.

source.place: Tag 09LT, with 09LN and both parts of 09KY

proof.text: To check naturality for any derived $M\to M'$ and $Y\to Y'$, choose projective models $P,P'$ and injective models $I,I'$. The localization comparisons give unique homotopy classes $P\to P'$ and $I\to I'$ representing the conjugated derived arrows. The two naturality squares for the composite in step 4 reduce to naturality of chain currying and of localization. The same argument for identities on the derived objects compares different choices of replacements, so the bijections are canonical. The natural-bijection statement now gives $T_N\dashv U_N$, with unit the transpose of $1_{T_NM}$ and counit the inverse transpose of $1_{U_NY}$. For simultaneous shifts use $P[k]$ and $I[k]$ as the replacements: projectivity and injectivity persist since their defining Hom acyclicity tests are shifted tests. The shift identity in the homotopy-calculus statement makes the step-4 composite commute with shifts. Applying it to those two identity morphisms proves the required shift squares for unit and counit. Exactness from step 3 already proves preservation of distinguished triangles.
